accepted.title: Achalasia treatment when operative rescue is prohibitive

record.title: Achalasia treatment when operative rescue is prohibitive

cues.phrase: a brief sedated endoscopy acceptable but describes prolonged general anesthesia and a major rescue operation as prohibitive
cues.why: The assessment strongly directs risk-based selection, but it is a necessary constraint rather than a gratuitous permission sentence. All labels are endoscopic. Choosing injection over dilation still requires knowing the latter's perforation/rescue implications; a wording-only match does not settle that close comparison.

fairness: The failed contractions, impaired relaxation and retained contrast support the motor/outflow disorder. The resident must then apply both anesthesia and rescue constraints: an endoscopic approach is not automatically suitable merely because it avoids a planned operation.

Botulinum toxin is the defensible best offered initial procedure for the represented risk assessment. Pneumatic dilation is the meaningful near-miss because the patient cannot tolerate major rescue if perforation occurs. The myotomy alternative requires a different anesthesia burden. Age alone is not the discriminator.

The named patient, age, sex, symptoms and complete task agree. This standalone node has no missing predecessor. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the constructed perioperative assessment still requires exact clinical sign-off.

This is high-yield treatment-selection reasoning. The combination of a motor diagnosis and procedure-specific rescue risk earns two consequential steps, although the explicit anesthesia assessment keeps it moderate rather than hard.
suggestions: Preserve the decision-critical rescue restriction. Do not remove it in an effort to make the item harder or replace it with age-based eligibility.

For future feedback refinement, explicitly explain why dilation remains a poor choice despite being endoscopic: its perforation risk can require rescue the patient cannot tolerate. Any wording change would be a new exact version requiring review.

after.Presentation: {patientName}, an 81-year-old woman, attends clinic because food and drinks pause behind the sternum and increasingly limit her meals.
after.Current update: Endoscopy and cardia imaging show no structural lesion. Adequate manometry shows failed body contractions with impaired junction relaxation, and the timed contrast study retains liquid above the junction. She has oxygen-dependent lung disease. The anesthesia record considers a brief sedated endoscopy acceptable but describes prolonged general anesthesia and a major rescue operation as prohibitive.
after.Task: Which initial procedure best fits {patientName}'s swallowing findings and perioperative assessment?
Options: **KEY:** Endoscopic botulinum toxin injection at the sphincter
Endoscopic pneumatic dilation of the junction
Endoscopic peroral myotomy of the distal junction

accepted.explanation: The motor and clearance findings support a junction-relaxation disorder, but treatment selection also depends on anesthesia and rescue risk. Botulinum toxin is the appropriate offered initial symptom-relief option for this risk profile. Age alone does not determine that choice.

accepted.title: Preserved propagation with elevated junction pressure

record.title: Preserved propagation with elevated junction pressure
fairness: The resident must interpret preserved propagation alongside elevated positional relaxation and intrabolus pressures, then recognize that symptom reproduction during manometry does not itself establish clinically relevant obstruction. Timed barium with a tablet is the best offered complementary assessment.

Solid-meal manometry is a real competing physiologic investigation, not simply a repeat of the completed liquid-swallow series. The adequate symptom-reproducing pressure study makes independent passage assessment more informative for the present unresolved issue. Meal provocation can provide supportive information; the explanation should not be read as claiming it is never useful in this pattern.

The absence of an explanatory endoscopic lesion, opioid use and prior foregut surgery addresses important confounders without supplying the diagnosis. No invented numerical cutoff is needed to solve this represented pattern. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.

The standalone presentation and task are complete. Distinguishing an outflow-obstruction pattern from conclusive achalasia and selecting confirmatory testing is relevant general-surgery motility content; this high-yield judgment is qualitative, not a verified exam-frequency claim.
The options use comparable investigation labels. No unique phrase match, diagnosis label, teaching sentence, absolute or common-component pattern selects the key without clinical knowledge.
suggestions: Retain the distinction between supportive symptom/pressure observations and complementary evidence of obstruction.
Keep the meal-provocation explanation qualified: its lower priority here does not make it generally useless in evaluating outflow-obstruction patterns.

cues.phrase: no mass or focal wall abnormality / Endoscopic ultrasound of the cardia and junction wall
cues.why: The negative wall finding lexically weakens the wall-imaging option. This is a residual elimination cue, but structural observations and the gradual stable-weight course are needed to rank further structural evaluation fairly. They do not exclude occult infiltration with certainty, and the final choice still requires understanding which physiologic assessment is feasible after failed manometry.

fairness: The acquisition history makes clear that crossing the junction was achieved but did not yield usable swallow recordings. The resident must avoid treating attempted placement as a completed physiologic test, then select FLIP to assess junction opening and motor response in the setting of demonstrated retention.

FLIP is the best offered next test. EUS remains plausible when occult secondary obstruction is suspected, but the gradual course, stable weight and described structural assessment lower that priority here. They do not prove that every infiltrative process has been excluded. Reflux monitoring does not resolve the demonstrated retention and missing motor assessment.

The explanation appropriately limits FLIP: it does not supply a complete pressure-based subtype or independently authorize irreversible treatment. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Exact test-priority verification was not performed because network and source review are outside this task.

The standalone node gives sufficient chronology and a complete task. No prior answer is needed. The present diagnostic competitors are different investigations, and the key is not merely the only untried test.

This is a useful advanced niche within a high-yield disease area. The precise FLIP-after-failed-assisted-manometry decision is narrower than commonly tested achalasia diagnosis and treatment; unfamiliarity with FLIP should not be mistaken for hard reasoning.
suggestions: Retain as optional advanced coverage rather than use it to satisfy core high-yield or hard-item targets.
Preserve the distinction between lower suspicion for a wall lesion and exclusion of secondary disease. Keep the failed acquisition observations and FLIP limitations explicit.

claims.statement: Failed peristalsis with relaxation measurements at the upper normal limit can leave achalasia unresolved and justify complementary testing in dysphagia.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: Lyon Wireless pH monitoring: AET <4.0% on all days with negative symptom association.

claims.statement: Negative off-therapy reflux testing supports discontinuing an empiric PPI when no separate indication remains.

claims.verificationLocator: ACG refractory-GERD key concepts 1 and normal-testing recommendation.

claims.statement: Baclofen requires objective GERD evidence, and prokinetic treatment for GERD requires documented gastroparesis rather than symptoms alone.

claims.verificationLocator: ACG medical-management recommendations against baclofen without objective GERD and prokinetics without gastroparesis.

claims.statement: A lesion-free columnar-lined segment under 1 cm is not routinely entered into Barrett surveillance, even after an incidental metaplasia biopsy.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG recommendation 2 and evidence summary; AGA 2025 abstract results.

claims.statement: Established nondysplastic Barrett in a treatment-suitable patient is generally managed with endoscopic surveillance.
claims.limitation: Conditional recommendation. No fixed interval, survival benefit guarantee or lifelong mandate is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: ACG surveillance recommendations; AGA 2025 abstract.

claims.statement: Routine prophylactic ablation is not the treatment pathway for established nondysplastic Barrett.
claims.limitation: Historical explicit wording checked against current surveillance/EET pathway. Same-society publications are not independent corroboration; AGA 2024 full-text access was unavailable.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: Historical ACG recommendation 30; current ACG surveillance and EET eligibility sections.

claims.statement: Confirmed high-grade Barrett dysplasia after careful lesion assessment is an indication for endoscopic eradication therapy rather than routine surveillance.
claims.limitation: Same-society cross-check only; not independent evidence. Esophagectomy may be appropriate for invasive/high-risk disease outside this specific flat-HGD context.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: Current ACG recommendation 17 and historical recommendation 30.

claims.statement: Anemia plausibly attributable to a type II-IV hiatal hernia can make the hernia symptomatic and justify offering repair to a fit patient.
claims.limitation: Expert opinion, not a universal mandate. Alternative bleeding sources and operative risk must be assessed; exact Cameron-lesion causal certainty requires clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ2 expert opinion; no invented hemoglobin or ferritin threshold.

claims.statement: Observation is reasonable for a truly asymptomatic type II-IV hernia after unrevealing workup and an informed discussion of acute-complication risk.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.
claims.verificationLocator: SAGES KQ2 expert opinion.

claims.statement: Selected patients with a nonischemic herniated stomach who cannot tolerate definitive reconstruction may undergo limited gastric fixation.

claims.statement: Gastric erosions at the diaphragmatic contact region can contribute to chronic iron loss in large hiatal hernias, but causal attribution requires excluding other sources.

claims.statement: Concurrent displacement of the gastroesophageal junction and gastric fundus above the diaphragm describes type III hiatal anatomy.

claims.statement: Fundoplication can be added to type II-IV hernia repair to address reflux, with a tradeoff involving postoperative dysphagia.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated in a foregut clinic; constructed record details define each narrower population.

claims.statement: Preprocedural high-resolution manometry checks for achalasia and absent contractility; normal swallowing or barium transit does not replace it.

claims.verificationLocator: Prescribing information section 5.12

claims.statement: Candida recovered directly on first access to a normally sterile postoperative intra-abdominal collection can be clinically significant when infection persists; a longstanding drain culture has a different evidentiary meaning.
claims.limitation: Conditional synthesis of invasive intra-abdominal Candida and drain-colonization guidance. Bloodstream recovery is not required by this atom; neither every drain yeast isolate nor an isolated screening test proves invasion.

claims.statement: An intravenous echinocandin is a usual initial treatment for invasive candidiasis in an adult while species susceptibility is evaluated.
claims.limitation: No dose, antifungal duration, eye/CNS treatment, device-removal rule or susceptibility breakpoint is authored.

claims.verificationLocator: CDC treatment overview. GAIS invasive candidiasis discussion.

claims.statement: Initial fluconazole is less suitable when severe invasive Candida infection is present and susceptibility is uncertain; non-albicans species and recent azole exposure increase concern that an azole will not provide reliable initial therapy.

claims.statement: Continuing or recurrent abdominal infection after source-control treatment requires reassessment for an uncontrolled focus and microbiological mismatch.

claims.statement: Antibiotics plus image-guided drainage should be considered for a large accessible diverticular abscess.

claims.statement: A small diverticular abscess in a clinically stable patient can be managed initially with antibiotics and close reassessment.

claims.statement: Worsening clinical infection with inadequate nonoperative source control supports operative management of diverticulitis.

claims.statement: Restoring continuity with a proximal diverting stoma is a reasonable reconstruction after emergency diverticular resection in a selected stable patient with suitable bowel and host conditions.

claims.statement: Hartmann reconstruction is supported for diffuse diverticular peritonitis in a critically ill patient or a patient with substantial comorbidity.
claims.limitation: WSES directly recommends this approach in the high-risk population. The exact clinical ranking still needs clinician review. Damage-control surgery may be another approach in physiologic extremis and is not excluded by this claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Selected physiologically unstable patients with diffuse diverticular peritonitis may need abbreviated source control and staged reconstruction.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. This supports a counterfactual and a scope boundary, not a claim that Hartmann is the only option during physiologic extremis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Segmental bowel-wall thickening and adjacent fat inflammation without a collection or uncontained perforation can represent uncomplicated diverticulitis.

claims.statement: Immunocompromise changes uncomplicated-diverticulitis antibiotic eligibility and supports antimicrobial treatment.

claims.statement: Selected stable immunocompetent, nonfrail outpatients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, oral tolerance and dependable reassessment may be treated without antibiotics.
claims.limitation: This is selective omission. The recommendations do not prohibit antibiotics for every uncomplicated case.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate is a listed treatment option when antibiotics are selected for acute uncomplicated diverticulitis.
claims.limitation: One directly checked society highlight supports the named regimen. No dose or treatment-duration rule is authored. Allergy, renal function, local resistance and oral tolerance still matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: The ACG-listed oral ciprofloxacin diverticulitis regimen includes metronidazole rather than ciprofloxacin monotherapy; WSES guidance supports enteric Gram-negative and anaerobic coverage when high-risk uncomplicated diverticulitis needs antibiotics.
claims.limitation: No dose, duration, admission rule, transplant-specific interaction clearance or local susceptibility guarantee is established. These require clinical assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context; constructed observations create no new clinical threshold.

claims.statement: CTA can localize a suspected lower-GI source during ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia when colonoscopy preparation is unsuitable.
claims.limitation: Current recommendation checked through the official guideline-author presentation. High suspicion for an upper-GI source must be addressed. This is not a universal CTA-first rule for stable or resolved bleeding.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Adequate bowel preparation improves the suitability of colonoscopy for identifying and treating a lower-GI bleeding lesion.
claims.limitation: No preparation volume, rate or fixed time is taught. The 2016 routine urgent-colonoscopy recommendation is excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: Tagged red-cell scintigraphy can be useful in selected intermittent obscure overt gastrointestinal bleeding.
claims.limitation: Historical guideline. It is not used to claim a universal current ranking over CTA or colonoscopy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Active colonic contrast extravasation on CTA supports prompt angiographic assessment with possible embolization.
claims.limitation: Experienced centers may also use colonoscopic hemostasis in selected circumstances. The constructed case retains brisk bleeding and intolerance of preparation to distinguish the routes.

claims.statement: Surgery after failed endoscopic and radiologic control should use careful anatomic localization to avoid leaving the culprit colonic segment in place.
claims.limitation: Single directly accessed historical society guideline for the exact surgical boundary. No universal subtotal-versus-segmental outcome advantage is asserted. Dense diverticula elsewhere do not establish bleeding origin.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated diverticular disease or lower-GI hemorrhage care phase and constraints.

claims.statement: A new intraluminal contrast focus appearing during arterial acquisition and accumulating on a later phase is compatible with active gastrointestinal contrast extravasation.
claims.limitation: Verified through the official guideline-author CTA discussion. This packet uses original written report observations and reproduces no scan or figure.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated diagnostic or treatment context and the explicitly described counterfactual.

claims.statement: Recurrent severe lower-GI bleeding after attempted endoscopic hemostasis can require radiologic therapy.
claims.limitation: Repeat colonoscopy remains reasonable in some stable prepared patients. The constructed recurrence is brisk and the colon is again obscured by blood.

claims.statement: A bleeding location suggested only by delayed tagged-red-cell images should be confirmed before directing segmental colonic resection.
claims.limitation: One directly accessed historical society guideline supplies this specific reliability principle. It does not establish an automatic operation when genuinely discordant current high-quality localization remains unresolved.

claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the represented clinic chart review; fictional current findings are observations, not empirical weights.
claims.verificationLocator: JSGE BQ3-(2)-5; distinguish failed extraction from failed access.

claims.statement: Duct stones can be cleared endoscopically or surgically; route selection depends on anatomy, expertise and the clinical setting.
claims.limitation: Apply within the specified population and stated care phase; guidance is not a probability rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the represented gallbladder or duct-stone condition; fictional clinic chart-review applications.
claims.verificationLocator: ESGE surgical treatment section; WSES 2.8

claims.statement: Informed watchful waiting can be offered to selected men with an asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic reducible inguinal hernia.
claims.limitation: Does not extend to femoral hernias or establish that every groin pain is caused by the image; symptoms may later lead to surgery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Coexisting hernia and musculoskeletal findings require symptom, site and activity correlation before assigning the functional limitation to the hernia.
claims.limitation: Case-specific reasoning from constructed observations; no validated symptom-attribution score or exclusive diagnosis is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A demonstrated inguinal hernia with concordant activity-limiting symptoms supports elective repair planning.
claims.limitation: Referral is not a promise to cure coexisting musculoskeletal pain or a ranking of all operations.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Clinical assessment with targeted ultrasound is appropriate when a suspected groin or recurrent hernia is not established on examination.
claims.limitation: Operator dependent; scanning the wrong location or not provoking an intermittent event does not establish absence at the symptomatic target.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A femoral hernia passes beneath the inguinal ligament through the compartment medial to the femoral vein.
claims.limitation: Anatomical relationship, not diagnostic accuracy or a patient-specific probability.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Entrapment of part of a bowel wall can threaten that wall while the remaining lumen continues to permit intestinal passage.
claims.limitation: One verified case report/discussion reused offline from the harden1 ledger; supports the mechanism, not quantitative risk or comparative efficacy. Original source and clinical verification dates retained.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Reduced contrast enhancement of trapped bowel wall on CT is concerning for bowel compromise in an acute hernia.
claims.limitation: WSES discusses reduced CT wall enhancement as a predictor; it is not alone proof of irreversible necrosis. No sensitivity, specificity or numeric cutoff is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Suspected strangulation in an acutely irreducible groin hernia supports emergency operative evaluation instead of manual reduction.
claims.limitation: Recommendations are strong despite low evidence; normal passage or an isolated normal biochemical result cannot resolve clinical ischemia concern.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A gentle manual reduction attempt can be considered for acute irreducibility when there is no suspicion of bowel ischemia; failed reduction requires emergency surgery.
claims.limitation: One current guideline, weak underlying evidence; hospital chart-review scenario, not authorization for forceful or unsupported office reduction.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A stable reducible femoral hernia warrants timely elective repair assessment rather than applying the selected-male inguinal watchful-waiting policy.
claims.limitation: No exact deadline or universal operative method is asserted; evidence is largely observational.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: For a stable patient with gross enteric contamination and a small groin defect suitable for closure, primary tissue repair is supported.
claims.limitation: One older guideline, grade 2C; its small-defect recommendation uses less than 3 cm. No broad rule for large contaminated ventral defects or biologic mesh superiority.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Bowel resection without gross enteric spillage does not automatically exclude a permanent macroporous synthetic mesh groin repair.
claims.limitation: HerniaSurge 2023 is a weak recommendation. Mesh is a permissible option, not a compulsory operation in every case; evidence overlaps WSES.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: An indirect inguinal sac enters lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels at the deep ring; a direct defect protrudes medial to those vessels through the posterior inguinal wall.
claims.limitation: Cord fat distally does not by itself establish the proximal route.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Chronic postrepair groin pain can include neuropathic and nonneuropathic components, so new mechanical findings require renewed anatomical assessment.
claims.limitation: Phenotypic assessment is not proof of one injured named nerve. Recurrence and non-hernia sources must be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Diagnostic nerve blocks may contribute to chronic postoperative groin-pain evaluation but transient relief is not a unique proof of cause or a guarantee of surgical benefit.
claims.limitation: One current guideline, very-low/low evidence. No universal response threshold or single-block surgery-selection rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Persisting diagnostic uncertainty after examination and ultrasound can justify dynamic MRI or CT; CT is an alternative when MRI is not possible.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline family; no universal MRI priority over hip assessment or diagnostic block, and no claim that MRI always resolves all pain sources.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: A posterior repair is recommended for a recurrent inguinal hernia after a prior anterior mesh repair.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline. Does not establish TEP superiority to TAPP; operative records, expertise and prior pelvic surgery matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: An anterior mesh repair is recommended for a recurrence after a prior posterior TEP or TAPP repair.
claims.limitation: One directly verified guideline; an incision described as open is not sufficient to identify the implanted mesh compartment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Mesh repair is recommended for most adults; an expert Shouldice repair remains a supported selected non-mesh option after informed choice.
claims.limitation: Does not establish all-patient equivalence of tissue and mesh operations or rank a surgeon without the relevant expertise.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Contrast-enhanced CT can contribute to assessment of suspected bowel compromise when the clinical assessment of an acute groin episode is uncertain.
claims.limitation: WSES addresses predictors of strangulation with low-quality evidence; it does not mandate CT before every reduction attempt or verify a universal timing threshold. The exact taxis-versus-CT ranking remains a clinician-review application of this and reduction-selection claims.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

claims.statement: Local anesthesia is supported for open repair of a reducible inguinal hernia by experienced teams and can benefit frail patients.
claims.limitation: Strong general local-anesthesia recommendation; frail-patient comparative evidence is weaker. Exact anesthetic drugs or doses are outside scope.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Prior pelvic or prostatic surgery and the need for local anesthesia can favor an anterior open approach over routine laparo-endoscopic repair.
claims.limitation: Not an absolute contraindication to expert laparoscopy and not a universal superiority claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults within the stated groin-hernia or postrepair-pain scenario; no pediatric extrapolation.

claims.statement: Prior prostatic or pelvic surgery is a reason to individualize the usual primary laparo-endoscopic repair preference and can favor an anterior open approach.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current guideline family; this is a relative planning consideration, not an absolute prohibition on expert TEP/TAPP. Combine separately with the experienced-team local-open claim for the exact cooperative patient; no universal postoperative technique ranking is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed groin-repair or postrepair-pain scenario; not a universal diagnostic or operative ranking.

claims.statement: Preventive NIV immediately after planned extubation can benefit selected high-risk adults, including patients with chronic respiratory disease and hypercapnia.
claims.limitation: Conditional evidence; not a mandate for all extubations or proof of superiority to every modern HFNC/NIV combination. Options deliberately do not rank NIV against an equally supported high-risk HFNC regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

claims.statement: Bilevel NIV is recommended for acute or acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis from a COPD exacerbation in a patient not requiring immediate intubation.
claims.limitation: Direct pH at or below 7.35, elevated PaCO2 and persistent tachypnea support the constructed record; not extrapolated to every hypoxemic process.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

claims.statement: Tolerating an SBT does not establish readiness for extubation when weak cough and abundant secretions impair airway clearance.
claims.limitation: Single guideline introduction directly states this boundary; no invented suction-frequency or cough-flow cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

claims.statement: SBT readiness assessment considers recovery, oxygenation, hemodynamics and spontaneous effort; an RSBI calculation is not required to authorize a trial.
claims.limitation: One direct guideline; no universal safety-screen cutoff authored. An abnormal isolated index is not a reason to bypass the rest of assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

claims.statement: Increasing FiO2 during an SBT can conceal an oxygenation limitation, so the trial should generally retain its baseline oxygen concentration.
claims.limitation: Conditional very-low-certainty recommendation based on indirect evidence; repeat unchanged-support trial is a context-bound author application, not a universal extubation algorithm.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated outside-hospital record; clinic encounter is retrospective review.

claims.statement: An adult spontaneous breathing trial may use low pressure support or no pressure support.
claims.limitation: Conditional guideline recommendation; a specific unsupported trial must still be assessed for actual oxygenation, effort and circulatory tolerance. This does not establish a universal best support protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adult outside-hospital ventilation record reviewed retrospectively in the clinic; context-specific author application.

claims.statement: An achieved arterial-pressure target does not establish adequate cardiac output or tissue perfusion.
claims.limitation: Interpret serial perfusion, flow and ventricular findings together. No isolated catheter value diagnoses the shock mechanism.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Dobutamine added to norepinephrine is an option for septic cardiac dysfunction with ongoing hypoperfusion despite adequate pressure and volume assessment.
claims.limitation: Very-low-certainty SSC recommendation. Epinephrine is another supported strategy. This packet does not offer both as mutually exclusive keys or claim a survival benefit.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Dynamic flow response is more useful than static filling pressure for predicting a cardiac-output response to further volume expansion.
claims.limitation: Predicting a cardiac-output response does not establish clinical benefit or a mandate to give fluid.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: A positive preload-response test requires a separate assessment of hypoperfusion and fluid-related harm before a bolus is chosen.
claims.limitation: Risk-benefit assessment is individualized. No source establishes the numerical patient observations as a universal treatment cutoff.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Norepinephrine is the preferred initial vasopressor for septic shock with persistent hypotension and preserved cardiac systolic function.
claims.limitation: SSC 2026 allows either norepinephrine or epinephrine with concomitant cardiac dysfunction. These initial cases explicitly retain preserved systolic function.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Persistent lactate elevation should be interpreted with serial perfusion findings and should not automatically trigger additional fluid.
claims.limitation: Continue reassessment. Improved peripheral signs do not certify resolution of every cause of hyperlactatemia. The case also supplies falling lactate and absent flow response.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: An initial MAP target of 65 mm Hg is supported for most adults receiving vasopressors for septic shock.
claims.limitation: SSC 2026 suggests 60–65 mm Hg in adults aged at least 65 years. The scored target case is 60 years old. Chronic hypertension and organ response require individual review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Higher vasopressor-driven pressure targets can add arrhythmia risk without a demonstrated patient-specific perfusion benefit.
claims.limitation: A higher target can help selected patients. The constructed target trial shows no organ-perfusion improvement and new atrial fibrillation. No universal rule to lower pressure in every arrhythmia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Adding vasopressin is supported when norepinephrine requirements escalate during septic shock.
claims.limitation: Conditional escalation strategy. No universal norepinephrine dose or compulsory sequence for all shock phenotypes is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing acute hospital shock assessment and resuscitation

claims.statement: Oliguria requires assessment of current perfusion, losses and accumulated fluid before choosing further volume treatment.
claims.limitation: Urine volume by itself does not establish hypovolemia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Loop diuretics can address volume overload during AKI when a response remains achievable.
claims.limitation: A diuretic response does not establish repair of renal tissue. Reassess the actual response.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Further fluid loading can worsen renal and systemic congestion when expansion is no longer needed.
claims.limitation: Edema can coexist with intravascular depletion. Current perfusion assessment governs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Kidney-replacement initiation depends on current complications and treatment response rather than an isolated creatinine result.
claims.limitation: Deferral requires close surveillance. This claim supplies no universal waiting period.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: AKI-associated pulmonary fluid accumulation with continuing major hypoxemia despite adequate medical treatment supports urgent kidney replacement.
claims.limitation: The current pulmonary-edema recommendation is panel opinion with low-certainty evidence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Creatinine and urine-output trajectories should be integrated with the clinical course when assessing AKI.
claims.limitation: Creatinine lags changes in filtration and is affected by fluid distribution and treatment clearance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Furosemide response testing can inform AKI progression assessment.
claims.limitation: This prognostic role does not replace complication- and response-based assessment for current kidney replacement.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: A thiazide can augment loop-diuretic treatment when congestion persists with loop resistance.
claims.limitation: Combination therapy is a credible competing strategy. It does not override the urgent RRT indication established by refractory major hypoxemia. No dose is prescribed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Loop agents and their administration routes differ in pharmacokinetics, which can affect the diuretic response.
claims.limitation: An agent or route change is a credible nonurgent consideration. No universal superiority or dose conversion is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with surgical or general critical illness and AKI. Pediatric and chronic maintenance-dialysis decisions are excluded.

claims.statement: Post-traumatic hepatic arterial pseudoaneurysm is treated with angiography/embolization; hemobilia after liver trauma can indicate this complication.
claims.limitation: WSES supplies the specific pseudoaneurysm recommendation; EAST independently supports angiographic management of hepatic complications but not every exact pseudoaneurysm criterion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: Persistent circulatory deterioration after resuscitation together with intraperitoneal fluid on FAST supports urgent trauma laparotomy rather than transport for CT.
claims.limitation: A transient pressure rise does not establish sustained stabilization; this claim does not choose among hybrid-suite interventions in a sustained responder.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: Angiography with embolization is an option for stable hepatic arterial extravasation; unstable nonresponders need operative hemorrhage control.
claims.limitation: Do not infer that every transient responder is eligible for transport or that all liver bleeding is arterial.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: Persistent traumatic biliary leakage may require endoscopic stenting in addition to drainage; diffuse bile peritonitis or failed minimally invasive control may require surgery.
claims.limitation: The presence of a collection alone does not prove a major duct disruption or mandate resection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: Multiphase trauma CT can distinguish an enlarging pool of extravasated arterial contrast from a contained vascular sac that follows blood-pool enhancement.
claims.limitation: One guideline supports active-versus-contained vascular interpretation. The constructed report is text, not a simulated scan or a performance claim.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specific abdominal/pelvic injury and care phase described in the mapped draft.

claims.statement: In a stable fully staged renal injury, isolated urinary extravasation without another operative indication is compatible with initial nonoperative monitoring.
claims.limitation: One adequate guideline; excludes suspected renal-pelvis/proximal-ureter avulsion, infection, obstructed drainage or persistent symptomatic collection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: A nonresolving or symptomatic post-traumatic urinoma may require ureteral stenting or percutaneous drainage.
claims.limitation: One guideline; does not rank stenting versus drainage for every collection or prescribe a size threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: When an expanding renal hematoma requires intervention, kidney-preserving techniques are conditionally favored over automatic nephrectomy when feasible.
claims.limitation: Conditional low-quality evidence; life-saving nephrectomy remains possible when repair cannot control hemorrhage.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: Delayed excretory imaging evaluates urinary extravasation and ureteral continuity beyond the arterial and venous trauma CT phases.
claims.limitation: One guideline publication; does not require an invented acquisition delay or presume a missing series was never acquired.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with abdominal or pelvic trauma in a trauma-capable hospital.

claims.statement: A focal small-bowel caliber change with upstream dilation and downstream collapse supports a mechanical obstruction.
claims.limitation: Distribution alone does not establish cause or bowel viability.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: A new concerning clinical course after an earlier reassuring SBO assessment requires renewed assessment for complications.
claims.limitation: A stable nonperitoneal patient with a new unresolved perfusion question differs from a patient with an established indication for immediate exploration.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Intravenous contrast-enhanced CT can assess bowel-wall enhancement when perfusion is a clinical concern in SBO.
claims.limitation: The exact acquisition is chosen for the clinical question. Imaging cannot guarantee exclusion of ischemia and must not delay treatment of clear peritonitis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: A lactate value in the laboratory reference interval does not exclude bowel ischemia.
claims.limitation: Serial clinical and imaging findings determine concern. No laboratory cutoff is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: In an adequately performed enteral water-soluble contrast assessment for adhesive SBO, failure to reach the colon by the 24-hour film strongly suggests nonoperative failure.
claims.limitation: Technical adequacy and clinical trajectory matter. This is not an isolated automatic operation deadline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: A closed-loop configuration, especially with reduced mural enhancement or associated fluid, warrants prompt operative assessment for threatened bowel.
claims.limitation: The questions combine anatomy with perfusion findings. A single minor fluid finding is not a universal operation threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Progressive or persistent right-sided abdominal pain after negative imaging can warrant exploratory laparoscopy for appendicitis or another cause.
claims.limitation: WSES recommendation 1.12 directly supports exploration after a progressive clinical course. NIDDK corroborates surgery for ongoing symptoms only at a general level. An adequate negative examination initially supports observation. The 2025 WSES exact update was unavailable for permitted full-text verification.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with unresolved right iliac fossa symptoms after cross-sectional evaluation and serial assessment.

claims.statement: A limited appendiceal tissue sample does not establish the final classification of the unsampled lesion; permanent assessment of the complete resection specimen informs candidacy for regional oncologic resection.
claims.limitation: Targeted check of ASCRS 2025 recommendation 2 and epithelial classification. The fictional specimen map demonstrates a separate infiltrative focus; no probability of sampling error is asserted. One adequate directly verified guideline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Appendiceal neoplasm after a limited outside review and complete permanent specimen review.

claims.statement: Infiltrative malignant glands distinguish appendiceal adenocarcinoma from a noninfiltrative low-grade mucinous neoplasm.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline. A fully evaluated permanent specimen is supplied in the draft. A small biopsy or uncertain frozen section would not establish the same extent.
claims.applicablePopulation: Permanent pathology assessment of an appendectomy specimen.

claims.statement: Nonmetastatic appendiceal adenocarcinoma generally warrants oncologic right hemicolectomy with regional nodal assessment.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 13. The draft has invasion into mesoappendiceal fat, adequate staging and a fit patient. The recommendation is not generalized to isolated LAMN or disseminated peritoneal disease.
claims.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with invasive appendiceal adenocarcinoma and no distant or peritoneal metastases.

claims.statement: Appendectomy is sufficient surgical treatment for a margin-negative LAMN with an intact wall and no peritoneal involvement.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 12. Used for counterfactuals and the boundary against invasive carcinoma. Surveillance details remain outside the scored task.
claims.applicablePopulation: Completely resected, nonperforated LAMN without peritoneal disease.

claims.statement: Selected patients with appendiceal mucinous neoplasia and peritoneal dissemination merit peritoneal-surface surgical assessment for cytoreduction and intraperitoneal treatment.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendations 13-15. Right colectomy does not by itself address diffuse peritoneal disease. Systemic chemotherapy has limited activity in low-grade disease. Referral does not assert that every patient is operable or requires one HIPEC regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: A fit patient with biopsy-confirmed low-grade appendiceal mucinous peritoneal disease and no distant solid-organ metastases.

claims.statement: Interval appendectomy is favored after complicated appendicitis in an older adult with persistent imaging suspicion for appendiceal neoplasia.
claims.limitation: Conditional guidance. The case has resolved infection, a focal residual nodule and a free appendiceal base. Normal cecal mucosa does not supply histology of that mural nodule. Exact timing and a universal younger-adult rule are withheld.
claims.applicablePopulation: An older adult after successful nonoperative treatment of appendiceal abscess with a suspicious persistent lesion.

claims.statement: An abnormal appendix encountered incidentally can be removed intact with a grossly clear base, preserving definitive specimen assessment before deciding on oncologic colectomy.
claims.limitation: One directly verified current specialty guideline, recommendation 2. The base and extent govern resection. Suspected mucinous lesions require avoidance of rupture. No automatic operation is specified for extensive peritoneal disease.
claims.applicablePopulation: An incidentally dilated, unruptured appendix with a separable uninvolved base and no peritoneal deposits.

claims.statement: An older adult recovering from an appendiceal abscess warrants evaluation for an underlying appendiceal or colonic neoplasm.
claims.limitation: The drafted patient is 62 with a persistent focal appendiceal abnormality. No age threshold or mandatory policy for all younger adults is keyed. The publications differ on routine interval appendectomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults after nonoperative treatment of complicated appendicitis, especially older patients or those with suspicious interval imaging.

claims.statement: Sac enlargement with uncertain leak origin requires investigation for occult type I or III inflow.
claims.limitation: Catheter angiography with possible cone-beam CT can resolve inconclusive CTA; no disputed growth cutoff is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Enlarging post-EVAR sac.

claims.statement: Retrograde flow from aortic side branches can fill the excluded sac.
claims.limitation: Type II physiology; other inflow sources must be assessed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR branch-associated flow.

claims.statement: Sealing a dissection entry can expand the true lumen and relieve dynamic branch obstruction.
claims.limitation: Single current specialty standard; response must be reassessed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Dynamic malperfusion treated with TEVAR.

claims.statement: Persistent fixed branch narrowing after central true-lumen expansion may require branch stenting.
claims.limitation: Single specialty standard; the case supplies persistent gradient and flap extension rather than assuming every residual image needs treatment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Residual static branch malperfusion.

claims.statement: An isolated type II endoleak with stable sac size can undergo imaging follow-up.
claims.limitation: Single publication; requires exclusion of higher-pressure leaks and continued surveillance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with stable post-EVAR sac.

claims.statement: Attachment-site flow into an excluded sac represents a sealing failure.
claims.limitation: Type I origin; one directly checked specialty standard.
claims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR sac opacification.

claims.statement: An established type I endoleak warrants prompt correction of the seal.
claims.limitation: Cuff extension requires an available healthy landing segment; complex cases may need other repair. One directly checked publication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Persistent or late attachment leak.

claims.statement: Surgery is appropriate for chronic-pancreatitis pain not relieved by endoscopic treatment.
claims.limitation: No universal time-to-surgery cutoff or superiority among all head-resection techniques inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy can decompress a dilated obstructed pancreatic duct; morphology guides operation selection.
claims.limitation: Normal-sized head and absence of a suspicious focal lesion are constructed operative-selection observations, not new numerical eligibility thresholds.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Pancreatic enzymes treat insufficiency but are not established treatment for chronic pancreatic ductal pain.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: An enhancing mural nodule at least 5 mm or main duct at least 10 mm is a high-risk IPMN finding supporting surgical evaluation in a fit patient.
claims.limitation: High-risk findings are not a cancer diagnosis. Operation and extent require multidisciplinary review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Imaging suggests cyst subtype but cannot establish histology or exclude malignancy.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: EUS with selective sampling can resolve management-relevant uncertainty after cross-sectional cyst imaging.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A body-tail cyst without duct communication in a woman is compatible with MCN; the pattern is not definitive histology.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A surgically fit patient with a presumed MCN at least 4 cm warrants resection consideration, especially with attributable symptoms or suspicious features.
claims.limitation: The exact 4-cm decision is directly supported by SIRM-AISP; ACG corroborates specialist evaluation, not this exact cutoff. No automatic cancer diagnosis or mandatory splenectomy inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Cyst-fluid CEA supports mucinous classification but does not grade dysplasia or diagnose cancer.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified guideline statement; a scant cytology sample also cannot establish a whole-cyst negative.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A cyst documented before a first pancreatitis attack cannot be attributed to that later attack as its origin.
claims.limitation: Chronologic inference, not proof of neoplasia; prior pancreatitis/chronic disease must be checked.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Larger pancreatic NETs with nodal-risk concerns generally favor formal resection with regional node assessment over enucleation.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Expert criteria favor enucleation of suitable small pancreatic NETs more than 2-3 mm from the main duct.
claims.limitation: Single consensus based on expert opinion; the fictional 1-mm and 6-mm observations are compared with this supported range, not introduced as new cutoffs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Initial surveillance is acceptable for selected asymptomatic nonfunctioning pancreatic NETs smaller than 1 cm.
claims.limitation: Single surgical consensus; not a mandatory rule or permission to observe symptomatic, growing or higher-risk lesions. The 1-2 cm zone remains individualized.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A limited pancreatic NET sample can underestimate grade because the tumor may be heterogeneous.
claims.limitation: Single consensus review of sampling studies; it does not imply every old low-grade result is incorrect.
